thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Remain in Positive Territory as Inflation Data in Focus, Trade War Fears Fade

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Remain in Positive Territory as Inflation Data in Focus, Trade War Fears Fade
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Thursday's regular session:
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.3%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +1.5%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.8%
United States Oil Fund ( USO ): -0.1%
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): +2.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 1.4%.
US stocks were higher, recovering nearly all of Wednesday's losses, as Wall Street's appetite for risk improved on signs China is willing to make concessions to avert a trade war with the US. Wall Street also took some comfort by mostly benign inflation data.
The Consumer Price Index for June rose 0.1%, below forecasts for a 0.2% increase over May levels. Excluding food and energy costs, CPI rose 0.2% in June in line with estimates. On a year-over-year basis, total CPI was up 2.9% and the core CPI was up 2.3%.
Meanwhile, first-time jobless benefit applications totaled 214,000 versus economists' expectations for a drop of 6,000 initial claims to 225,000 applicants, remaining near multi-decade lows.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 1.4% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were in the green.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 1.01% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.4%.
Apple (AAPL) rose 3% after it released updates for its MacBook Pro laptop, featuring a touch bar and faster Intel (INTC) core processors along with a quieter keyboard. The updated 13-inch model has a starting price tag of $1,799, while the 15-inch type costs at least $2,399, the Cupertino, California-based technology giant said on Thursday. Both models are available online and in stores later in the week.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 1% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 1.1%.
Virtus Investment Partners (VRTS) rose some 1% after it said that its preliminary total assets under management (AUM) as of June 30 increased 2.8% from the period ended March 31 to $91.6 billion. Long-term AUM increased 2.7% from the same period to $89.8 billion.
Energy
Dow Jones U.S. Energy Fund (IYE) was down 0.05% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.03%.
Ferrellgas Partners (FGP) fell more than 1% after it said on that it acquired Diamond Propane, a propane retailer based in Potsdam, N.Y. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive and allows the partnership to strategically grow its footprint in northern New York. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Commodities
Crude was down 1%. United States Oil Fund ( USO ) was down 0.1%. Natural gas was down 0.7% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.7%.
Gold was up 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.4%. Silver was up 1.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 1.2%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.04% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were higher.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.7% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were weaker.
The Buckle (BKE) fell almost 9% after it said that June same-store sales fell 1.2% while net sales slumped 3.8% to $70.9 million from the same month last year.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.9% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was 1.2% higher.
AcelRx Pharmaceuticals (ACRX) shares slumped nearly 13% after the company said it priced an underwritten public offering of almost 7.3 million shares at $2.75 each, equal to a 19.1% discount relative to the stock's Wednesday closing price. The company also granted underwriters a 30-day option to acquire up to nearly 1.1 million shares. The company expects gross proceeds of $20 million and plans to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes. The offering is slated to close on or about July 16.
